title: fix(app-shell): a record page's delete asks through the console's own confirm dialog (objectui#11001)
body:
Fixes #11001
Clause-②: no

## What changed

On a record page, More actions then Delete asked through the browser's native `window.confirm`. The header's `sys_delete` action in `packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx` now awaits `confirmHandler(msg)`: the page's own promise-based confirm handler, the one it already hands the action runner as `onConfirm`, which opens the in-app `ActionConfirmDialog`. That is the same dialog the list view's delete opens: app-shell's `ObjectView` hands `useConsoleActionRuntime`'s confirm handler to `useObjectActions` as `onConfirm`, and the runner calls it with the delete question. Confirm runs the existing delete unchanged (`dataSource.delete`, the success toast, back to the object's list). Cancel returns before anything runs, so the record and the page stay as they are.

- The question is the page's existing `detail.deleteConfirmation`. The dialog's title and buttons are its defaults (`actionConfirm.title`, `actionConfirm.confirm`, `actionConfirm.cancel`), exactly what the list view's delete shows, because both callers pass one argument. **No pack key is added**, so this is not serial behind objectui#11039.
- Two comments said the handler had exactly one caller (the runner): the `ConfirmationHandler` note above `confirmHandler` in `RecordDetailView.tsx`, and the header of `RecordDetailView.confirmRuntimeParity-5835.test.tsx`. This change made both false, so both now name the second caller. That test file is outside the claim's declared file surface; the edit is comment-only, and the file's tests ran green (below).

## Premises checked on `origin/main` `827550193`

1. The `sys_delete` action's `onClick` in `RecordDetailView.tsx` called `if (!window.confirm(msg)) return;`. Confirmed.
2. app-shell's `ObjectView` hands `actionRuntime.confirmHandler` to `useObjectActions` as `onConfirm` and renders `actionRuntime.dialogs`, which include `ActionConfirmDialog`. Confirmed; the row delete goes through `actions.deleteRecord`, then the runner, then that handler with one argument.
3. `useObjectActions` documents `onConfirm` as falling back to `window.confirm`. The record page does not mount that hook. It already owns a handler of the same published `ConfirmationHandler` type feeding the same `ActionConfirmDialog` (parity pinned by `RecordDetailView.confirmRuntimeParity-5835.test.tsx`), so the seam used is that existing handler, not a second hook mount.
4. `detail.deleteConfirmation` and the three `actionConfirm` keys exist in all ten packs.

## Pin

`packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.deleteConfirmDialog-11001.test.tsx` mounts the real record page under a real `I18nProvider` (en) with the REAL `ActionConfirmDialog`, opens the header overflow and chooses Delete. Every test installs a `window.confirm` spy that answers yes, so the old code would delete at once with no dialog.

- The `alertdialog` opens carrying `detail.deleteConfirmation` and the dialog's default buttons; nothing is deleted yet; the spy is not called.
- Continue: `dataSource.delete` is called once with the object and record id, one success toast, and the router leaves for the object's list.
- Cancel: the dialog closes, no delete, no success toast, and the router location is unchanged.

Strings are read from the `en` pack by key, not written out.

## Verification (final commit `64c0db025`)

- `pnpm exec vitest run` over every test file that names `RecordDetailView` (104 files: all 37 `RecordDetailView.*` pins, 36 existing plus the new one; the three app-shell ratchets that read it; `useConsoleActionRuntime.test.tsx`; the console and package tests that mention it): `Test Files 104 passed (104)`, `Tests 1028 passed (1028)`.
- Ablation, with the fix committed first. The mutation went through `ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor hits 1 then 0, blob changed) and was restored to the HEAD blob with `git diff HEAD` empty. With `if (!window.confirm(msg)) return;` put back, the new pin reads `Tests 3 failed (3)`, each `Unable to find role="alertdialog"`. Run at `a537ec3e7` and again at `64c0db025`, same result. No build or dist step is involved: the pin imports `./RecordDetailView` from source.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): exit 0, after building the `@object-ui/app-shell^...` closure with turbo (28 of 28 tasks). `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFilesOnly` lists the new pin and the edited parity test.
- `pnpm exec eslint --format json` on the three changed `.tsx` files: 3 files, 0 errors. Narrowing proof: the population is the `**/*.{ts,tsx}` block of `eslint.config.js`; no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService` is set, so linting is not type-aware and this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file. Warnings on the two edited files are unchanged from the base (111 and 17, read through `--stdin` at `827550193`).
- Exit 0: `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-changeset-overwrite`, `check-changeset-claims` (report-only; it names `.changeset/7997-detail-view-related-retired.md` because that body mentions `RecordDetailView.tsx`; its paragraph is about the retired `DetailView` schema mirror and this change does not touch that), `check-control-bytes`, `check-new-cross-file-line-citations` (0 new), `check-vi-mock-specifiers`, `check-vi-mock-inherit`, `check-vi-mock-override-shape`, `check-test-path-roots`, `check-type-check-coverage`, `check-lint-coverage`, `check:i18n-keys`, `check:handler-key-reads`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`. `check-governed-queue-guard --test` over the four paths: NOT GOVERNED.
- Declared narrowing: the whole `packages/app-shell/src/views/` directory (565 test files) was NOT run locally. The 104-file set took about 6 minutes under the shared lock, so the directory would not fit the 10-minute foreground cap; CI's sharded `pnpm test` runs all of it. The set run is every test file that names `RecordDetailView`; a test that reaches the page only through a transitive import, without naming it, is not in it.

## Acceptance notes

- Read-only observation, not filed: the record page's Delete does not go through the shared `recordDelete` core in `@object-ui/core` (objectui#10383) that the list view's delete uses. So for a package-owned `sys_permission_set` row (ADR-0094) the record page would ask the plain delete question and toast "Record deleted" where the list view asks the reset question. Not measured on a live page, and whether the record page offers Delete on that object at all was not checked. Carrier: none.
